_about.purpose: Real hospital financial-assistance facts the agent can cite on a call, instead of asking open-endedly whether 'any programs' exist. US nonprofit hospitals must publish a Financial Assistance Policy under IRS 501(r), so this is public information.
_about.verification: Every hospital entry marked verified:true was read from the hospital's own published policy, not from a summary site. Several aggregator sites publishing 'hospital financial assistance 2026' guides were checked and found to misstate thresholds - one reported Mass General Brigham as offering free care under 300% FPL when the published policy says discounts of 60% or more. Do not add entries from those sites.
_about.no_public_corpus: There is no bulk machine-readable dataset of FAP terms. The Lown Institute has reviewed ~2,500 hospitals but publishes per-hospital pages, not a download. Entries here are added by hand from primary sources.

federal_poverty_guidelines.note: Hospital thresholds are expressed as a percentage of these figures. This table is what converts '300% FPL' into a dollar number for a specific household, which is the single most useful thing the agent can do with it.

national_priors.source: Lown Institute, hospital financial assistance and debt collection policies report (sample of ~2,500 hospitals, data collected June 2024 - April 2025), https://lownhospitalsindex.org/report-hospital-financial-assistance-and-debt-collection-policies/
national_priors.note: Use these when the specific hospital is unknown. They let the agent say what is *typical* and ask the rep to confirm their own figure, which is far stronger than asking whether a program exists at all.

hospitals.name: Mass General Brigham
hospitals.hardship_provision: Patients above the income threshold may still qualify if medical bills exceed 40% of annual income.
hospitals.quotable: Discounts of 60% or more may be available for medically necessary care for patients whose income is less than 300% of the Federal Poverty Guideline. Higher income patients may qualify if their medical bills are over 40% of their annual income.
hospitals.note: Do NOT describe this as free care under 300% FPL - the published policy says discounts of 60% or more, which is different. Several summary sites get this wrong.

hospitals.name: Cleveland Clinic
hospitals.quotable: Family income up to 400% of the Federal Poverty Level is considered for the Financial Assistance Program.
hospitals.note: Public page states the 400% ceiling only; the free-care threshold and sliding-scale bands live in the downloadable policy PDF and are not yet captured here. Cooperating with Medicaid screening is a stated precondition.

levers._note: Program types worth naming explicitly on a call. Naming a specific mechanism is what separates this from 'do you have any programs?'
items: Charity care / financial assistance under the hospital's 501(r) policy
Sliding-scale discount for income above the free-care threshold
Medical hardship or catastrophic provision keyed to bills as a share of income, which applies even at higher incomes
Itemized bill review for billing and coding errors
Amounts Generally Billed cap - 501(r)(5) forbids charging FAP-eligible patients more than amounts generally billed to insured patients
Retroactive application to an already-billed or already-in-collections account
